findings.title: Loading a song with playback stopped (and Clear Song) cuts the drone off hard and brings it back in hard
findings.scenario: Drone running, playback stopped, load a song. load_song_ui.cpp:269 and clear_song.cpp:83 call deleteOldSongBeforeLoadingNew(), which sets currentSong = NULL in deluge.cpp:1076. readFromFile keeps calling routineWithClusterLoading(), so renderAudio runs, but renderDrone returns immediately when !currentSong. The drone breaks off in the middle of the wave (click) and stays silent during the whole load. The voices keep gainL/R at full level. So on the first render with the new song they come in abruptly at full volume (second click). If the new song has no drone, they come back briefly and then fade out. This also contradicts the comment "keeps what's sounding across songs". The same pattern with stem export: renderAudioForStemExport leaves out the drone, so it freezes at full level and comes back in hard after the export.
findings.fix: Keep rendering the drone without a song too, as long as drone.isSounding() holds. Either with a static DroneSettings in which all tones are inactive (fades out via kFade within a few blocks). Or with a copy of the last rendered settings and the last context volume, so it keeps sounding through the load. For stem export, fade out before the start or call drone.reset(), so that it restarts from silence afterwards.

findings.title: With external clock the position jumps in whole ticks, and synced beats wobble
findings.scenario: With external clock, getCurrentInternalTickCount sets timeRemainder = 0 (playback_handler.cpp:1146, "TODO") and truncates the float position to whole ticks. So context.position is constant within a tick and then jumps by one tick. Example: magnitude 1 (48 ticks per quarter), sync 1/64. The target of the beat phase jumps by about 1/6 cycle per tick. lockCorrection pulls in a quarter of that every block, which is of the order of the beat increment itself. The beat rate is thereby modulated periodically, and the pulsing becomes audibly uneven (above all isochronic and binaural).
findings.fix: If isExternalClockActive(), take the fractional tick position directly: make getCurrentInternalTickFloatFollowingExternalClock() public or offer a public accessor for it. Separately, the factor in the lockCorrection gain can be lowered with external clock.

findings.title: Tempo and position use different tick magnitudes
findings.scenario: quarterNotesPerSecond comes from calculateBPM(), which only takes insideWorldTickMagnitude into account. context.position, by contrast, divides by getQuarterNoteLength(), which also includes insideWorldTickMagnitudeOffsetFromBPM. The offset is not 0 when a sync scaling clip is set (song.cpp:835-849). Then the lock target runs faster or slower than the beat frequency by the factor 2^offset, lockCorrection stays permanently at the clamp limit ±0.5·halfBeat, and the synced beat wobbles instead of locking in.
findings.fix: Derive both from the same basis: quarterNotesPerSecond = 44100.f / (getTimePerInternalTickFloat() * currentSong->getQuarterNoteLength()). The metronome also counts on this basis (playback_handler.cpp:889).

checkedWithoutFinding:
Checked with no finding:
- XML reading and writing: attributes of the drone tag plus self-closing tone child tags in the same pattern as reverb/compressor, exitTag pairs correct. The tag is in the default branch of the switch ("dron" collides with no case). If the tag is missing, the defaults from the fresh song apply. Clamping of all tone fields is fine, and index is checked.
- The syncLevel round trip is consistent (writeAbsoluteSyncLevelToFile and convertSyncLevelFromFileValueToInternalValue respectively). inputTickMagnitude is an attribute and is read first.
- 1.2.1 cleanly skips the unknown tag with its children: globalEffectable returns RESULT_TAG_UNUSED, tryReadingFirmwareTagFromFile too, then exitTag.
- SideChain::render returns values from -ONE_Q31 to 0. So gain and duck lie between 0 and 1, and registerHit is used as for the reverb. The SideChain constructor in the song ctor finds no dangling preLoadedSong (it is set to NULL after the swap and in the error path).
- Song volume: context.volume lies between 0 and 4. Even 16 tones at -12 dB, hard-panned and with volume 4, give around 9.5e7 and so do not overflow int32.
- calculateBPMForDisplay in the stopped state takes the song tempo. timePerInternalTickMovingAverage is preset when the external clock starts.
- currentSong swap during playback: the voices glide over. initTables runs in AudioEngine::init before the first render, plus the tablesReady guard.
- Stem export excludes the drone. BSS around 26.7 KB, 4 KB double sine on the stack at boot, the song grows by about 700 B.
- aligned_buf.h: the stdint include is harmless. noteToHz clamps note and cents; the phase increments do not overflow.

reason:
Confirmed. I traced the finding in the code; it is not tested on hardware.

Sequence when loading with playback stopped (load_song_ui.cpp:269) and on Clear Song (clear_song.cpp:83): deleteOldSongBeforeLoadingNew() (deluge.cpp:1076) sets currentSong = NULL. During loading, routineWithClusterLoading() keeps calling renderAudio() via AudioEngine::routine() (audio_engine.cpp:398). renderDrone (audio_engine.cpp:870) returns immediately when !currentSong. drone.reset() is not called anywhere in the whole tree.

1) Break-off at the start: the tone breaks off in the middle of the wave. But unassignAllVoices(true) also cuts all synth voices off hard, so this matches the firmware's previous behavior. On its own this is a small flaw.

2) Re-entry after loading: this is the real bug. The voices keep started = true as well as gainL/gainR and level at full level. renderVoice (drone.cpp:320) starts the ramp at voice.gainL, so in the first sample it jumps from 0 to full level (click).
- New song with the same drone: hard entry instead of a glide.
- New song without a drone, or Clear Song (tones inactive): the old drone comes back at full level for a few blocks and then fades out with kFade = 0.5 per 128-sample block. That is an audible blip of about 10 to 30 ms. Only then is started set to false (drone.cpp:423).

This contradicts the comment in audio_engine.cpp:153. On a song swap during playback currentSong is never NULL; there it works correctly.

Stem export: renderAudioForStemExport leaves out renderDrone. The state freezes and comes back in hard after the export. This is real, but only a side case.

Fix: in renderDrone, when !currentSong, render with a static DroneSettings in which all tones are inactive, as long as drone.isSounding() holds. The drone then fades out within a few blocks during loading, and the new song starts from silence. Alternatively call drone.reset() in deleteOldSongBeforeLoadingNew: the break-off at the start then stays, but the entry starts from silence with a glide. Also call drone.reset() before the stem export.

The mechanism is right, but the audible effect is not. With external clock, getCurrentInternalTickCount sets the remainder to 0 (playback_handler.cpp:1146) and truncates the float position to whole ticks (line 1149). So context.position is stair-shaped; audio_engine.cpp:879ff. computes with timeSinceLastTick=0.

Why it is still hardly audible:
- The error is limited to at most 1 tick. At 120 BPM that is 5.2 ms with the default magnitude 2 (96 PPQN, flash_storage.cpp:311) and 10.4 ms at magnitude 1.
- lockCorrection (drone.cpp:309) acts as a first-order low-pass, limited to ±50% of the rate.
- The audio engine cuts the render windows at every swung tick (audio_engine.cpp:766f.). So the error pattern is almost the same per tick and runs periodically with the tick rate. At sync 1/64 that is an integer multiple of the beat rate (3 or 6 ticks per beat). So every pulse is distorted the same way. That is not uneven.

I simulated the lock loop with sync 7, 120 BPM and blocks of 32/80/128 samples that are cut at the ticks:
- 96 PPQN: on average 1.5–2.6 ms delay, jitter 0.4–1.0 ms peak to peak.
- 48 PPQN: on average 4–6 ms delay, jitter 1.4–2.3 ms peak to peak.

At 48 PPQN the rate modulation does reach the ±50% limit, as claimed. But the phase deviation of the half beat stays at about ±0.02 cycles (PM sidebands around −25 dB at the tick rate). A timing error of around 1 ms with pulses at 32 Hz is no audible wobble. With slower syncs the error in ms stays the same and is negligible relative to the pulse duration.

What remains is a constant delay of about half a tick against the grid. That is below the jitter that MIDI clock brings anyway.

To show it as a real bug, you would need a recording on the device with external clock, magnitude 1, sync 1/64 and isochronic or binaural mode, with measurably irregular pulse onsets or audible roughness compared with the internal clock.

The proposed fix is still clean and cheap, as an improvement: with isExternalClockActive(), use getCurrentInternalTickFloatFollowingExternalClock() publicly.

findings.title: MIDI Follow has no case for UIType::DRONE, so CCs go to the last clip instead of the song
findings.scenario: MIDI Follow is on and the user has been inside any clip earlier. In Drone view, getSelectedClip() falls through to `default: clip = getCurrentClip()`. An external controller's CCs (and their feedback) then change that clip's params. In Song view the same CCs change the song's global FX.
findings.fix: Add `case UIType::DRONE: break;` (clip stays nullptr), the same as Song view with no clip held.

findings.title: Undo/redo from Drone view casts DroneView to TimelineView
findings.scenario: The user zooms or scrolls in Song view, opens Drone view and sends a MIDI-learned UNDO or REDO. allowedToDoReversion() is true because the current UI is the root. revertAction picks SCROLL or ZOOM, and lines 539/555 call `((TimelineView*)getCurrentUI())->initiateXScroll/initiateXZoom` on DroneView, which is not a TimelineView. That is a wrong vtable call and can crash.
findings.fix: Guard both calls with `getCurrentUI()->toTimelineView()` and set the animation to NONE otherwise, or return false from allowedToDoReversion while the root is droneView.

findings.title: The Drone item is also reachable from the Song menu in Arranger and arranger-Automation, but exit always goes to Song view
findings.scenario: The same Song menu opens from arrangerView and arranger automationView. Opening Drone from arranger automation and pressing Back leads to Song view with automationView.onArrangerView still true, so a later clip automation view opens in arranger mode. From Arranger, goToSongView's xScroll/xZoom restore is also skipped.
findings.fix: Give OpenView an isRelevant() that returns `getRootUI()==&sessionView`, or remember the previous root and leave to it through the proper transition.

findings.title: Back LED keeps blinking after the drone menu closes
findings.scenario: SoundEditor::setLedStates blinks BACK. SessionView (line 175), Arranger and Performance clear it in focusRegained. DroneView::focusRegained does not, so the LED blinks until the user leaves the view.

findings.title: On 7-segment models the beat and pan values are not visible
findings.scenario: Turning the lower knob calls changed(false). On 7-segment that shows the pitch, so the beat or sync value never appears. The pan popup "Pan -32" is cut to four characters ("PAn "), so the number is lost.
findings.fix: On 7-segment, show a popup of the beat (or the sync division) after the lower knob turns, and use a number-only pan popup, as the level popup already does.

checkedWithoutFinding: Checked with no finding: SoundEditor::setup(nullptr, &droneToneMenu) (song mod controllable; the clip-null path is the same as Song view); the menu closing back to focusRegained; Shift+shortcut pads use paramShortcutsForSongView and reset currentSidechain through setup(); plain pad presses close the menu; SidechainMenu::beginSession sets droneSidechain, and nothing outside the editor reads currentSidechain. Also checked: all Selection option counts match their enums (4/2/8/4); ranges of Frequency/Beat/Note/Cents/Pan/Level; isRelevant; the one-string Submenu (title equals name); OpenView's exitCompletely followed by changeRootUI; SCALE_MODE in Song view (no earlier branch catches it, shift is excluded, stem export is blocked); view.buttonAction fallthrough (Save/Load/Shift+Select, Clip/Keyboard do nothing); renderingLock; OLED buffers; scroll and index clamping; setUIForLoadedSong; strings and 7-segment JSON. Minor: in the drone sidechain submenu the Song-view sidechain shortcut pads blink.

reason:
Refuted. The comparison with Song view does not hold in this 1.2.1 base. In src/deluge/io/midi/midi_follow.cpp there is no song context: getModelStackWithParam (line 197ff) only works when clip != nullptr. The UNPATCHED_GLOBAL cases (lines 287–330) belong to audio clips, not to the song FX. When getSelectedClip() returns nullptr in Song view without a held clip, getSelectedOrActiveClip() (lines 116–133) picks getCurrentClip()->output->getActiveClip(). This is intended, as the comment in line 121f also says: "we want to control the active clip". So in Song view, CCs already control the last entered clip or its active clip today, not the global song FX.

In DroneView (UIType::DRONE, drone_view.h:33), `default: clip = getCurrentClip()` applies in line 170f. That gives practically the same target as in Song view. midiCCReceived (line 468) and sendCCWithoutModelStackForMidiFollowFeedback (line 638) treat both cases the same. There is no crash, because a null clip is caught everywhere.

The fix `case UIType::DRONE: break;` therefore changes nothing in the result. clip becomes nullptr, and then the fallback in getSelectedOrActiveClip again picks the active clip of the same output. There is a small difference only when another clip is currently active on the output of the current clip (session: another clip of the same track launched). Then Drone view controls the currentClip and Song view the active clip. That is a cosmetic inconsistency and not the reported bug. Anyone who wants to align them can still add the case. But a real device symptom "CCs land in the clip instead of the song" does not arise, because Song view behaves the same way.

Confirmed. In audio_engine.cpp:876, qnps comes from calculateBPMForDisplay() → Song::calculateBPM (song.h:450-459). This function only computes with insideWorldTickMagnitude, so qnps = ticks/s ÷ (24·2^mag). context.position, by contrast, divides by getQuarterNoteLength() = 24<<(mag+offset) (song.cpp:5584, getInputTickMagnitude in song.h:184). So the position runs at qnps·2^-offset. The metronome also counts by getQuarterNoteLength (playback_handler.cpp:889).

The offset is reachable on the device. You press the sync scaling button on a clip (view.cpp:365), or a song with a saved sync scaling clip is loaded (song.cpp:2219). inputTickScalePotentiallyJustChanged (song.cpp:830-850) gives:
- loop with odd part 9 (3 bars, 6 bars, one 3/4 bar): offset = +2
- odd part 15 (5 bars): offset = +2
- odd part 1 (e.g. 128 ticks): offset = −2
Only clips with an odd part near 3 (1, 2, 4 bars) give 0. The time base itself (timePerTimerTick) stays unchanged.

The effect in drone.cpp:304-309: the voice runs at syncedBeatHz(qnps), but the lock target runs 2^offset times as fast or as slow. At offset = +2 it would need −0.75·halfBeat, but the clamp only allows ±0.5. So the phase error keeps growing and wraps around as int32. lockCorrection then jumps between −0.5 and +0.5, and the beating fluctuates between 0.5× and 1.5× instead of locking in. Even without the lock (stopped), the beat frequency does not fit the metronome grid.

Fix as proposed: context.quarterNotesPerSecond = 44100.f / (playbackHandler.getTimePerInternalTickFloat() * (float)currentSong->getQuarterNoteLength()). Check timePerTick > 0 first. That way position and tempo come from the same basis, and this also holds when stopped.

Confirmed. In the arranger automation view, pressing Select opens the song menu with `soundEditor.setup(nullptr)` (automation_view.cpp:2252-2253). This choice is made by sound_editor.cpp:1478, which checks for `currentUI == &automationView`, and the menu contains `&droneViewMenu` (menus.cpp:1456). `OpenView::selectButtonPress` (drone_view.cpp:487-491) switches to droneView without any check. `exitToSongView` (drone_view.cpp:194-196) always goes to sessionView. `automationView.onArrangerView` stays true, because only `handleSessionButtonAction` resets it (automation_view.cpp:1914-1915), and that is bypassed here. Neither `opened()` nor `initializeView()` nor `openedInBackground()` resets it.

Sequence on the device: Arranger, Shift+Song (arranger automation), Select, Drone, Back. You end up in Song view. There, open a clip and press Clip (instrument_clip_view.cpp:354). Or enter a clip whose `onAutomationClipView` is set. The automation view then runs in arranger mode. It shows the arranger parameters instead of the clip automation. Select opens the song menu instead of the clip menu (automation_view.cpp:2252). Song jumps to the arranger instead of Song view (automation_view.cpp:1914). playback_handler.cpp:200/318 and midi_follow.cpp:165 also behave as in the arranger. Coming from the normal arranger, the restore of xScroll/xZoom[NAVIGATION_CLIP] from `arrangerView.goToSongView` (arranger_view.cpp:173-176) is also missing. And you end up in Song view instead of the arranger you came from.

Fix, simplest: override `isRelevant()` in `OpenView` with `return getRootUI() == &sessionView;`. Alternative: remember the previous root UI in `DroneView::opened()`. When leaving, for arranger automation set `onArrangerView = false` and call `changeRootUI(&arrangerView)`. For the arranger, return directly to the arranger.

The finding is correct and occurs on the device. It needs a MIDI-learned UNDO or REDO. The Back button does not trigger undo in the drone view, because DroneView::buttonAction (drone_view.cpp:312) catches BACK itself, and there is no undoButtonX on the hardware.

Sequence:
- MIDI UNDO goes through playback_handler.cpp:2670 and slowRoutine:157. allowedToDoReversion() is true, because the current UI is the root UI and the UI mode is NONE.
- In revertAction none of the transition cases applies for the current UI droneView: DroneView is neither a ClipMinder nor sessionView, arrangerView, keyboardScreen or automationView.
- The else branch (action_logger.cpp:435) then compares xZoom/xScroll[NAVIGATION_CLIP] with the action's values. An example: notes edited in the clip view, then scrolled horizontally, then Song → Drone → MIDI UNDO. The comparison gives SCROLL or ZOOM, and line 539 or 555 casts droneView to TimelineView.

The effect is proven in the built ELF (build/Release/deluge.elf). TimelineView::initiateXScroll calls getNavSysId() via vtable+0x9c and setupScroll() via +0x98. The vtable of DroneView is only 0x94 bytes long (0x201b9a5c), and the vtable of AutomationView lies directly behind it. So getNavSysId() lands in AutomationView::horizontalEncoderAction and setupScroll() in AutomationView::buttonAction, each with this=&droneView. Their return value serves as an index into currentSong->xScroll[], and AutomationView fields are read beyond the small DroneView object. That leads to memory corruption or a crash. On the ZOOM path, calculateZoomPinSquares via an equally wrong slot comes on top.

Fix: in action_logger.cpp:435 replace `if (getCurrentUI() != &keyboardScreen)` with `if (getCurrentUI()->toTimelineView())`. keyboardScreen is not a TimelineView, so nothing changes for the existing views. whichAnimation then stays NONE, and xScroll is set directly in lines 532 and 541. This is not tied to the drone view, but protects against any root UI that is not a TimelineView. Alternatively, allowedToDoReversion() can return false while getRootUI()==&droneView. That also prevents an ENTER_AUTOMATION_VIEW or ClipMinder switch from leaving DroneView without exitToSongView.

The finding is correct. It is a pure LED bug without a crash or loss of state, but visible on the device.

Sequence in the code:
1. drone_view.cpp:331-332: pressing Select opens the menu via `soundEditor.setup(nullptr, &droneToneMenu)` and `openUI(&soundEditor)`.
2. sound_editor.cpp:258: `SoundEditor::setLedStates()` calls `indicator_leds::blinkLed(IndicatorLED::BACK)`. The default value numBlinks=255 means the LED blinks without end (indicator_leds.cpp:79-80).
3. Back at the top level: `goUpOneLevel()` leads to `exitCompletely()`, then to `close()` and `closeUI`, which calls `DroneView::focusRegained()` (ui.cpp:192). No step on this path stops the blinking.
4. `DroneView::focusRegained()` (drone_view.cpp:178-192) sets SYNTH, KIT, MIDI, CV, KEYBOARD, CROSS_SCREEN_EDIT, SESSION_VIEW and SCALE_MODE, but not BACK. `view.focusRegained()` does not touch BACK either. `setLedState(led, false)` would end the blinking via `stopLedBlinking` (indicator_leds.cpp:48-49), but is not called for BACK anywhere.
5. Only when leaving the view does `SessionView::focusRegained` clear the LED (session_view.cpp:175). Until then Back keeps blinking in the drone view.

To delimit it: the path via the menu item "Drone" in the song menu is not affected. `OpenView::selectButtonPress` calls `exitCompletely()` before the view changes. So `sessionView.focusRegained` runs first and clears BACK. Only the menu opened inside the drone view is affected. But that is exactly the normal way to edit a tone, so the bug occurs every time.

The proposed fix is correct: add the line `indicator_leds::setLedState(IndicatorLED::BACK, false);` to `DroneView::focusRegained()`, as SessionView (session_view.cpp:175) and ArrangerView (arranger_view.cpp:528) do.

Confirmed; both parts show on the device. There is no crash, but operation on 7-segment models is faulty.

1) Beat/sync (drone_view.cpp:420-431): the lower knob changes tone.sync or tone.beat and then only calls changed(false). On 7-segment that leads to showOnSevenSegment() (lines 211-221), and this function always shows only the pitch (note name or whole Hz). There is no popup in this branch. Pressing the lower knob only shows "SYNC"/"BEAT" (line 460), but no value. Result: the user turns the knob and sees no change. They can only reach the value via the menu (Beat/Sync in menu_item/drone/items.h:137/150).

2) Pan (lines 362-365): snprintf "Pan %d" goes to display->displayPopup(). SevenSegment::displayPopup calls encodeText with the default value limitToDisplayLength=true (seven_segment.h:91-92). When writing, it stops at writePos >= kNumericDisplayLength (seven_segment.cpp:~414). So "Pan -32" becomes "PAn ". The number is lost and no scrolling helps.

Side finding on the same mechanism: Shift + upper knob in Hz mode (hundredths) also shows no change on 7-segment, because showOnSevenSegment only shows whole Hz.

Fix: in the lower knob's branch, show a popup when !display->haveOLED(). With tone.sync>0 e.g. snprintf "%d" with (1 << (sync-1)), which gives the division 1/N as a number. Otherwise the beat in tenths (beat/10, max. 1000), with drawDot for the decimal place, e.g. displayPopup(buf, 3, true, 1). For pan, use a plain number as for level: display->haveOLED() ? "Pan %d" : "%d". Optionally, also show the Hz hundredths with Shift as a popup.
